title: We formalized GeneralPushPull
summary: The new development opens up κₜ (network gain), Dₜ (zero-sum influence operator), bₜ (closed-loop noise influence), and qₜ = ‖bₜ‖². Each quantity is constructed in Lean, making the route from the network dynamics to the effective node count explicit.

title: We formalized ADMM
summary: Two minimization steps and a multiplier update become one connected argument. Starting from Lan’s Section 3.7, the development follows subproblem optimality through telescoping bounds to objective error and constraint residuals.

title: We formalized RSGD
summary: A randomly selected iterate changes what an expectation must mean. The development makes the sampling history and output law explicit, connecting stochastic gradient updates to the expected gradient-norm bound in Lan’s Section 6.1.

title: We formalized the MARINA algorithm family
summary: Gradient differences save communication; adaptive queries make the probability argument harder. The formalization builds the generated estimator process and tracks the measurability and integrability needed for its expectations and variance recurrences.

source.label: Gorbunov, Burlachenko, Li & Richtárik · MARINA · arXiv:2102.07845

title: We formalized stochastic Push–Pull on time-varying digraphs
summary: Based on On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs. The development tracks periodic Perron weights and influence operators behind n_eff, including a period-two construction showing how temporal variation can break linear speedup.

title: We expanded SOptLib with network and tensor mathematics
summary: The October snapshot adds network-matrix theory for Push–Pull and tensor/operator-mean tools for adaptive preconditioning. Sampling identities, estimator-error recurrences, and descent lemmas become reusable parts of the shared library.

title: We formalized Muon and its corrected complexity results
summary: Formalizing the matrix optimizer exposed a counterexample to the printed Appendix B.4 branch. The released development proves corrected complexity results with an explicit cross-control condition, recording exactly where the source argument needs repair.

source.label: On the Convergence Analysis of Muon · arXiv:2505.23737v3

title: We formalized SDCS and extracted reusable library results
summary: Stochastic decentralized communication sliding couples local optimization with network consensus. The development connects the two expected bounds of Lan’s Theorem 8.11 and completes library extraction, with the source corrections and hypotheses recorded alongside the proofs.

title: We formalized Shampoo’s matrix, tensor, and diagonal variants
summary: The preconditioners are real matrices; a needed Mathlib inverse-order theorem lives in the C*-algebra interface. We bridge the representations for inverse-order and fractional-power inequalities, then connect matrix, tensor, and diagonal regret bounds under explicit hypotheses.

title: We released the first canonical SOptLib snapshot
summary: Proofs start sharing the mathematics that used to sit between the lines: sampling histories, stochastic oracles, Bregman geometry, and descent and complexity lemmas. The initial canonical snapshot brings that infrastructure together for later developments.
